le_latitude_deg, le_longitude_deg, he_latitude_deg, and he_longitude_deg sample ranges (e.g. -62.187801 to 82.512802, -179.881256 to 179.338837) fit a DECIMAL(9,6) representation without loss.

Runway end-point latitude, longitude, elevation, and heading fields carry null_rate between 0.22 and 0.28, and displaced-threshold fields carry null_rate 0.884 and 0.900, so all are retained nullable rather than imputed or dropped.

purpose: This table provides cleaned runway reference data sourced from the ourairports_runways bronze capture, describing each runway's physical dimensions, surface, lighting/closure status, and end-point geolocation and heading, keyed by runway id, to feed downstream airport infrastructure and flight-planning analyses.
usage: Consumers should join on the 'id' primary key or on 'airport_ref' to the airports table; latitude, longitude, elevation, heading, and displaced-threshold fields are populated only when the corresponding runway end was surveyed (null rates range from about 22% to 90%, with displaced-threshold fields the sparsest), so downstream queries must explicitly handle nulls rather than assume completeness.
limitations: Length, width, elevation, and displaced-threshold measures were narrowed from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER based on whole-number samples, discarding any fractional precision that might exist beyond the sampled rows; heading fields retained two-decimal precision instead. Latitude, longitude, elevation, heading, and displaced-threshold fields carry null rates from roughly 22% up to 90%, reflecting incomplete historical surveys, and were retained as nullable rather than imputed or row-dropped; airport_ref and airport_ident were not validated against the airports table in this cleanup.
